_comment: Which composite product each ramp reads, and what the measurement
found. A product reaches a legend and a readout only from a row here
with covered true, the same rule the per-radar coverage file applies.
Two checks stand behind each row, and a ramp ships only after both.
The first is validation_tests/visual/check_ramp_ticks.py, which reads
the bar's color at the row of each number printed beside it, puts that
color through the shipped invert.ts, and requires the band that comes
back to contain the printed number. That is what makes the bounds and
the axis shape evidence rather than a transcription: read as linear,
the accumulation bar reports 12.14 inches at its own 1.00 tick.
The second is validation_tests/visual/ramp_coverage.py against real
frames from the deployment. Full coverage is the rule for radar
frames, whose images are nothing but data. The composite PNGs are not:
they carry coastlines and boundaries drawn in near-black, and their
colors sit one or two units off the bar's, so 'pixels' here is the
share of painted area that reads back rather than a pass mark. A
product ships when its frames' common colors land on stops exactly,
which says the table is the right one, and unmatched colors then read
as nothing rather than as a wrong number.
Measured on 2026-11-21 against the test deployment.

products.note: Nowcast of the same field, published from the same colormap.
The frame's commonest colors sit on stops at distance 0. The rest is coastline drawn into the image and one-unit noise around each stop.

Built from prate_tools.py on the QPE tooling host: the same 12 anchors as the QPE products, but from_list with N=74 under a BoundaryNorm over a nine-segment edge array. Discrete, so every pixel is an exact entry and all 22 colours in ten painted frames read back. Both renders run, pcolormesh at line 112 and contourf at line 114 in the same colours, and it is the contourf fill that is read: it paints each band in one entry, which is where the exactness comes from. The field is gaussian_filter(sigma=1.0) smoothed before plotting, so a reading is a smoothed value, which the ramp's source line records. The earlier rejection said every frame fetched was transparent, which is the post-smoothing threshold of 0.003 in/h rather than a broken render. Units verified at the conversion site: HRRR prate arrives as kg/m2/s and the script multiplies by 141.732 for in/h against a true 141.73228, high by 0.0002%.
Nine distinct colors over a million painted pixels, all on stops.

Built from accum_tools.py and cumu_accum_tools.py on the forecast host, which the AQPI Backend session read on 2026-11-23. They use forecast rate's 12 anchors through from_list with N=68, under a BoundaryNorm over np.unique of seven linspace segments. Both renders run, and the contourf fill paints each band in one entry. Measured on 2026-11-23 against that day's 19Z frames from imageData, every opaque pixel sits exactly on a stop for both products in both units. The bar-read ramp this replaces read 57 to 62% of the same frames, because only 4 of the bar's 68 colors are colors the code paints. The field is smoothed (gaussian_filter, sigma 1.0) and masked below 0.003 in or 0.075 mm, so the first entry is never painted and the ramp drops it. Past the last edge the pcolormesh shows the last color, so the top band reads as 9.22 in (230.56 mm) or more. No measured frame reached that band.

The same ramp and the same renderer; plot_max_water_level.py:89 carries a colour block that is byte-identical to the level one.

Built from the renderer's own colormap: the same 12 anchors as the forecast rate but LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list with no N, so 256 entries, under LogNorm(0.01, 20). Read from qpe_new.py on the C-band producer host. The same table as the accumulation products with the unit changed, because the renderer uses one colormap for all three and only the label differs; a rate reported in inches is a rate reported wrong. The six intermediate values in its bounds list never reach the norm, so there are no bands in these images at all, which is why the block colorbar the catalog publishes explained so little of them. Neither renderer generates a bar. The remaining fifth of the pixels is matplotlib's antialiasing, where a pixel sits between two of the 256 entries and the per-stop tolerance refuses it. These three are unsmoothed: qpe_new.py imports gaussian_filter and never calls it, so the shortfall is resampling alone. One caveat on accuracy: qpe_new.py converts mm to inches with 0.0394 for accumulation and 0.03937 for rate, against a true 0.0393701, so accumulation reads 0.08% high and rate 0.0008% high.

Meters, from the bar's own label and confirmed on 2026-11-21. radarca's catalog says feet and backend/config.py followed it until this measurement.

Built from the renderer's own colormap, not from the published bar: LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list over 14 anchors, N=256, linear vmin=-4 vmax=10 metres, read from plot_water_level.py:108 on the CoSMoS host. The published colormap_level_ft.png is a hand-made asset with no code path to the plotter, which is why it verified against its own printed numbers and explained 0.032% of the pixels. The renderer resamples with a Hanning window, so most pixels sit between two of the 256 entries; the per-stop tolerance in invert.ts admits a neighbour only where that moves the answer by at most 1% of the range, which is 0.14 m. Two bands are dropped because the map turns back on itself below zero and paints -3.84 m and -2.41 m the same colour, and #6f00ff is dropped because the unmasked -99999 fill clips to vmin and lands on it.
